papers.title: Hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in the iron garnet Almandine Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$
papers.summary: Antiferromagnets on the hyperkagome lattice provide a three-dimensional route to strong magnetic frustration, but experimentally accessible realizations with well-established microscopic Hamiltonians remain scarce. Garnets are a broad family of materials in which magnetic ions can form two interpenetrating hyperkagome lattices, giving rise to spin glass, spin-liquid and hidden-order physics. Here we identify the iron aluminosilicate garnet almandine, Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$, as a spin-$2$ hyperkagome antiferromagnet. Using density functional theory energy mapping, we determine a Heisenberg Hamiltonian for the high-spin Fe$^{2+}$ moments and find dominant nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, as well as significant longer-range interactions. Classical Monte Carlo simulations of this Hamiltonian, combined with quantum-to-classical rescaling of the spin length, show a transition to antiferromagnetic order at $T_{\rm N}\approx9.8$K, in excellent agreement with specific heat experiments. The resulting non-collinear magnetic state is naturally described by magnetic toroidal octupolar order, which we connect to known results for the highly frustrated hyperkagome antiferromagnet gadolinium gallium garnet, Gd$_3$Ga$_5$O$_{12}$. We also calculate magnetic neutron diffraction amplitudes as well as static and dynamic structure factors using semiclassical dynamics, providing quantitative predictions for future neutron scattering experiments. Our results establish almandine as a chemically accessible realization of frustrated hyperkagome magnetism in the garnet family.

papers.title: Double quantum dots as dynamical impurities in one-dimensional transport
papers.summary: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. For a single impurity, we solve the scattering problem exactly and show Feshbach-like perfect elastic reflection, whose resonant condition distinguishes the initial two-level state. For several impurities in a strongly reflecting chain, transmission peaks at an intermediate mean level splitting. At small splittings, energy exchange with the impurities can weaken constructive interference between backscattered paths, consistent with the initial rise in transmission. As excitation channels close, virtual transitions can enhance reflection and drive transmission below its purely elastic value $T_0$. At larger splittings, these virtual processes weaken and transmission approaches $T_0$. We discuss how gate-controlled transmission measurements in quantum-dot arrays could test these predictions.

papers.title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
papers.summary: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

papers.title: Emptiness formation in quantum fluids: a hydrodynamic solution
papers.summary: We develop an auxiliary-kernel method for constructing the hydrodynamic instantons that govern macroscopic emptiness formation in one-dimensional Galilean quantum fluids. The key step is to represent the equation of state by an auxiliary integral kernel inspired by the Bethe ansatz. For equations of state admitting such a representation, we reduce the imaginary-time hydrodynamic problem to a single integral equation. Its solution determines the full density and current profiles, the vacuum boundary, and the leading emptiness rate. Notably, the construction does not require microscopic integrability. For the Lieb--Liniger gas, we derive the previously conjectured integral equation for the leading rate and use a known elliptic solution to obtain explicit expressions for the rate and vacuum boundary. Direct hydrodynamic numerics support the predicted boundary. We also recover known instanton solutions for a family of polytropic fluids.

papers.title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
papers.summary: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator. An agent designs its own experiments, uses a supplied simulator that may be under-resolved or physically wrong, and reports each property with a 95% interval. To our knowledge it is the first benchmark to combine agent-designed experiments, a deliberately flawed simulator, and proper scoring of calibrated intervals against exact ground truth. On a held-out split (93 tasks, 9 models, 2,511 episodes), models handle procedural traps. When the simulator is missing physics, most report wrong values while stating they are 95% sure: their ranges contain the truth in 20-62% of cases, against 94% for GPT-6 Astra and 99% for Claude Fable 5.2. At default effort the failing Claude 5.5 models rarely diagnose the missing physics (Opus in 35% of episodes, against 66% for Astra), and even when they do, their ranges often miss; Astra and Fable design experiments in which the flawed simulator is accurate, such as gentle heating, which keeps Astra calibrated even when it does not name the cause. Asking for wider intervals does not help; stating the strategy improves interval scores 1.6-2.5-fold, replicated on a pre-registered fresh split, but coverage barely moves. A pre-registered effort ablation shows that the correction is latent in the Claude 5.5 models: at maximum effort Opus improves more than tenfold and is no longer detectably behind Astra at default, but only with 13-31 times more reasoning; older and open-weight models gain nothing. Fable 5.2 is the most accurate model at default effort (interval score 1.9 times better than Astra's) but writes 6 times as many tokens, and at Astra's token count it falls short. We release the environment, graders and harness.

papers.title: Failure of Mean-Field Critical Scaling and Two Distinct Dissipation Regimes in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_{7-δ}$
papers.summary: Recently, superconductivity with an onset transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}$) up to 96 K has been observed in the $\mathrm{La}_{2-x}\mathrm{Sm}_{1+x}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-δ}$ system under pressure, providing an attractive platform for investigating superconducting mechanisms in nickelates. Here, we systematically analyzed the critical scaling and vortex dynamics for the $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{Sm}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-δ}$ single crystal with $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}=92.5$ K under pressure. Within the Ullah--Dorsey framework, neither the two-dimensional nor three-dimensional scaling provides a good collapse near $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{MF}}$. This failure may be associated with the multiband composite order parameter of bilayer nickelates, in which pairing is mainly driven by antiferromagnetic exchange in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital, whereas the superfluid stiffness is mainly governed by the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. The two-step decrease in the logarithmic resistivity reveals two distinct dissipative regimes. The low-temperature regime is well described by the thermally assisted flux flow (TAFF) model, whereas the high-temperature regime cannot be explained by the vortex dynamics involved with the superconducting fluctuation. The crossover between the two regimes may be associated with the orbital-dependent evolution of vortex cores. These results suggest the significant role of the composite order parameter in critical fluctuations and vortex-motion dissipation in nickelates.

papers.title: Local topology hallucinations in universal machine-learned interatomic potentials
papers.summary: Predicting metastable states with universal machine-learned interatomic potentials requires that they preserve the minima and saddles of the reference potential-energy surface. Here we identify local topology hallucination, in which distinct model minima relax into the same reference basin. This failure arises from mode-selective curvature-sign errors shared by MACE, CHGNet and M3GNet. Curvature signs predicted by two of the three models agreed with density-functional calculations in 55 of 57 positive but only 5 of 56 negative cases. In LiGe$_2$S, two MACE minima connected by a verified saddle relaxed into one density-functional basin. Reference relaxation likewise returned nine of ten selected model minima to their reference basins. A directional test with two displaced reference calculations rejected 9 of 12 prospectively tested model instabilities. Model agreement alone therefore cannot establish that predicted minima are distinct metastable states.

papers.title: A conditional quadrature method of moments for populations of oblate spheroidal particles
papers.summary: Non-spherical particle populations are encountered in numerous industrial processes, where particle size, shape, and velocity jointly influence transport, breakage, and classification dynamics. The resulting coupled distributions of geometric and kinematic particle properties evolve within a high-dimensional phase space whose accurate representation remains a significant challenge. We present a conditional quadrature method of moments (CQMOM) for oblate spheroidal particles described by a five-dimensional phase space that includes their size, aspect ratio, and velocity. The dimensionality of the problem is reduced by assuming that the particles continuously adopt their drag-maximizing orientation. In the solution algorithm, the resulting conditional quadrature representation of the particle phase space is combined with a Strang splitting of the continuous and discontinuous mathematical operators governing the moment transport. We verify this CQMOM framework against Monte Carlo simulations of the same particle model for representative test cases of increasing complexity, including drag, breakage, recoil, and attrition, at different Stokes numbers. With two nodes per coordinate, the particle number, the mean size, and the mean aspect ratio agree with the Monte Carlo solution within its statistical uncertainty, and the velocity statistics to within 7 %. Time-step and quadrature resolution studies identify the conditional velocity quadrature as the main source of the remaining deviations, for which we discuss potential remedies. Overall, the results demonstrate that the conditional quadrature representation preserves the geometric-kinematic correlations of the particle population in a five-dimensional phase space, at a cost more than 60 times lower than that of a single Monte Carlo realization.

papers.title: Renormalization group study of critical behavior of $O(m)$ model with cubic anisotropy and extended defects: two-loop approximation
papers.summary: We study the impact of quenched extended defects correlated in $ε_d$ dimensions and randomly distributed in the remaining $d - ε_d$ dimensions on the critical properties of a $d$-dimensional $O(m)$-symmetric system with cubic anisotropy. Exploiting the field-theoretic renormalization-group approach within the minimal subtraction scheme, we compute the two-loop renormalization-group functions. Applying resummation techniques to analyze the asymptotic series, we estimate the marginal values of $ε_d$ above which disorder becomes relevant for the physically important cases $m = 2$ and $m = 3$ in $d = 3$. We report numerical values of the critical exponents for the disorder-induced universality classes.

papers.title: Energy spectrum of trions in semiconductors
papers.summary: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schrödinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta $J=0$ and $J=1$ of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds. The dependencies of the energies on the mass ratio for trions in a bulk crystal qualitatively agree with the results for a simplified model of a trion in a 1D quantum wire, for which the three-body energies can be calculated with arbitrary precision as well as easily approximated using Born-Oppenheimer potential-energy curves. A comparison of our results with data from other publicly available three-body codes as well as with the energies of well-known atomic counterparts, in particular, with vibrational energy levels of the molecular hydrogen ion, shows a good agreement and confirms the accuracy of the numerical data. We found that GEM significantly improves the precision of the obtained trion energies compared to previous calculations. Our calculations demonstrate that, for most semiconductor compounds, only one trion state with zero total angular momentum exists.

papers.title: A spherical body in plasma simulated with adaptive mesh and algorithm refinement
papers.summary: An absorbing sphere in a weakly ionized plasma is the oldest kinetic problem of probe theory. It presents key difficulties in plasma simulation: disparate velocity scales, orbital motion, phase-space regions that no characteristic of the plasma reaches, a boundary set by a kinetic flux balance, and collisions that qualitatively change the answer. We use this problem to demonstrate the Plasma Adaptive Mesh and Algorithm Refinement (PAMAR) framework introduced in a companion paper. Electrons and ions have separate solvers on their own adaptive $(r,v,μ)$ octrees, or on reduced phase spaces at the angular-moment level (Fokker-Planck and two-stream models), coupled through a radial Poisson field solver. Two exact references, a method of characteristics for the collisionless problem and integration along the orbits for elastic scattering, audit the solvers. We compute the current-voltage characteristic of the probe on both electron and ion branches, and the profiles of the potential and of the moments of both species agree with the exact solution. Far from the sphere, the potential follows the Coulomb law in neither limit: it falls as $r^{-2}$ without collisions and as $r^{-1}$ only beyond the ion mean free path. With elastic electron scattering, the kinetic solver follows the exact dependence of the collected current on the mean free path, from free flight toward diffusion, to 1 percent. Finally, we demonstrate the ion model selection cell by cell, using a fluid model coupled to the kinetic solver, with the interface set by the pressure anisotropy; with charge exchange, a sensor of ion trapping is also needed. According to exact solutions, the ion anisotropy extends to several probe radii, much farther than the electron loss cone.

papers.title: Localization transition in a spin chain with an exact Fock-space tree
papers.summary: Many-body localization is often pictured as Anderson localization on the graph of many-body configurations. Strongly correlated disorder and a dense net of loops, however, make this graph hard to analyze. We introduce a local disordered spin-1 chain in which a single domain wall explores an exact binary tree of configurations. Random fields create strongly correlated disorder on this tree, as in generic interacting systems, while the absence of loops keeps the problem tractable. We rigorously bound the spreading of the domain wall at strong disorder, and efficient numerics on exponentially large trees indicate a localization transition at finite disorder strength.

papers.title: Variational Monte Carlo for Quantum Excited States via Nested Low-Rank Approximation
papers.summary: The electronic Schrödinger equation encodes a molecule's electronic structure and quantum properties, but solving it scales exponentially with the number of electrons. Solving this equation with neural-network variational Monte Carlo (VMC) has reached chemical accuracy on the ground state of small molecules; extending this success to excited states is constrained by two existing paradigms. Penalty-based methods need $K$ Laplacians per step but require tuning the overlap-penalty weights against the energy gaps they aim to compute. Natural excited states VMC (NES-VMC) is penalty-free, but it combines the $K$ ansatzes into one determinant, whose local energy requires $K^2$ Laplacians per step. We resolve this trade-off via low-rank approximation (LoRA) reparameterization of the rank-$K$ variational objective. The reparameterized objective admits a VMC-compatible stochastic gradient estimator via MCMC sampling from the per-state Born densities, and a sequential nesting scheme recovers the lowest $K$ eigenstates in eigenvalue order. The resulting algorithm, NestedLoRA-VMC, inherits a global optimality guarantee from the LoRA principle. On the first-row atoms Li through Ne at $K=10$, its accuracy is comparable to that of NES-VMC and of a state-of-the-art penalty-based method.

papers.title: Atomistic Insights into the All-Optical Switching of GdCo Alloys with Minimal Gd Concentration
papers.summary: Single-pulse all-optical helicity-independent switching (AO-HIS) is most commonly observed in Gd-based ferrimagnets near magnetization compensation. Recent experiments, however, demonstrated switching in Pt/Co/Pt-based heterostructures containing only a small amount of Gd at a Co/Pt interface. Here, we use atomistic spin-dynamics simulations to test an effective interfacial GdCo-alloy picture and to determine how species-dependent spin-bath coupling controls the minimum Gd concentration required for reversal. We compare a three-monolayer Co film with Gd confined to the surface layer and a three-dimensional uniformly alloyed GdCo model. Within the present uniform-heating model, robust transient toggle-like reversal is obtained far from compensation when the Gd coupling to the thermal bath is substantially weaker than that of Co; for λCo = 0.02 and λCo = 0.001, reversal occurs down to 1.5 at. % total Gd for selected pulse parameters. Increasing the Gd content accelerates reversal, consistent with the interpretation of Gd as an angular-momentum reservoir, whereas dilute interfacial Gd produces slower and more stochastic dynamics. These results show that compensation is not a fundamental requirement for ultrafast AO-HIS and identify the effective Gd spin-bath coupling as a key control parameter. Quantitative comparison with experiment will require explicit optical absorption, stack-dependent heat flow, dipolar fields, and a stable-final-state switching criterion.

papers.title: Self-attention is a Dyson equation for many-body machine learning
papers.summary: Why does symmetric sum-pooling (DeepSets) predict ground-state potentials to sub-meV accuracy, yet fail for correlated wavefunctions and excited states? Sum-pooling is a mean-field (Hartree) model: its $O(1/N)$ off-diagonal Jacobian suffices for nearsighted ground-state energies, but erases nonlocal two-body correlations. We show that self-attention is a real-space Dyson iteration whose Boltzmann (softmax) kernel acts as a two-body self-energy. Because physical Hamiltonians act pairwise, Löwdin's 2-RDM theorem and the Galitskii--Migdal relation guarantee that iterating a two-body propagator captures the full energetics of correlated matter. When fitting a fractal backflow determinant, DeepSets blurs the nodal surface onto a mean-field envelope, whereas self-attention recovers the fractal attractor. Seen through this lens, the unreasonable effectiveness of attention is not an accident; in a universe built from pairwise interactions, two-body attention is all you need.

papers.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
papers.summary: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the same device, we are able to explore different power ranges: from $-155\;$dBm to $-130\;$dBm for the directly coupled qubits and from $-95\;$dBm to $-55\;$dBm for the dispersively coupled qubits. When determining the microwave-line attenuation for a frequency of $6.0\;$GHz from room temperature to the millikelvin stage of the cryostat, we obtain best estimates and uncertainties for the directly coupled transmons of $(74.7\pm 0.2) \;$dB and for the dispersively coupled transmons of $(75.4\pm 6.8) \;$dB. The larger uncertainty of the dispersively coupled qubit measurements indicates that these qubits are less reliable for power sensing than the directly coupled qubits, most likely, due to the additional coupling resonator, whose transfer function is difficult to estimate accurately. Our results constitute the first step towards validation of qubit power sensing in dilution fridges, leading towards traceability for cryogenic microwave measurements.

papers.title: Accessing Electrode Edges: Upright Mounting for Site-Specific Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography of Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.summary: Cryogenic atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) is increasingly being used to map the three-dimensional distribution of highly reactive species in heterogeneous materials, including those found in battery systems. However, site-specific preparation of localised features and liquid-solid interfaces remains challenging, particularly when regions of interest (ROIs) are concentrated along electrode edges that are difficult to access using conventional mounting geometries. Here, we present a cryo-APT workflow incorporating an upright-mounting procedure that enables targeted specimen preparation of localised regions using plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) microscopy and milling under cryogenic conditions. We first demonstrate the approach using an electrolyte-wetted graphite electrode, successfully preparing and analysing a specimen containing both an edge-localised electrolyte deposit and the underlying graphite and Cu current collector. We then apply the workflow to a cycled graphite electrode, targeting Li dendrites concentrated around the electrode perimeter and successfully preparing and analysing the targeted Li-rich region. Beyond battery systems, this approach offers potential for site-specific cryo-APT of edge-localised features across a broader range of material systems, where conventional specimen preparation geometries may limit access to ROIs.

papers.title: Vortex states in submicron titanomagnetite particles
papers.summary: Numerical simulation is used to study the magnetic properties of spheroidal titanomagnetite particles Fe(3-x)TixO4 (0.4 < x < 0.6) with semi-axes ratio ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 and transverse diameters D = 100 - 480 nm. It is shown that various vortex micromagnetic states can emerge in the titanomagnetite particles depending on the titanium concentration, aspect ratio and particle diameter. The single-domain particle diameters are determined using the energy diagrams for stationary uniform and vortex states. The remanent magnetization of dilute assemblies of titanomagnetite particles with varying titanium content are calculated as a function of the transverse particle diameter D. It is demonstrated that for submicron-sized titanomagnetite particles, D ~ 500 nm, the normalized remanent magnetization of the assembly reaches very low values, M/Ms < 0.01, where Ms is the saturation magnetization of the particles.

papers.title: A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
papers.summary: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. At small wave vectors, we construct the correlation function by inverting the Ornstein-Zernike relation to approximate the structure factor of a hyperuniform pattern. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. We show that, for a fixed driving force, the specific structures and wave vectors selected by the density field can be controlled by modulating the width of the correlation kernel. Furthermore, we show that the scaling of the low-wave-vector region of the correlation function can accurately reproduce a specified hyperuniform exponent, independently of the structural properties at larger wave numbers. Our results establish a free-energy-based framework for describing disordered hyperuniform states, demonstrating and enabling independent control over structural selection and long-wavelength density correlations.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
papers.summary: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students. The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.

papers.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
papers.summary: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight. Equilibrium temperatures are given for both a theoretical lumped body and for a slab body, in which thermal conduction is considered. All data are limited to the solid state, up to a material-specific upper temperature limit. Currently, the database applies to extraterrestrial (AM0) sunlight only. A graphical App is also provided for exploring and visualizing the database.

papers.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
papers.summary: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

papers.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
papers.summary: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

papers.title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
papers.summary: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Martínez {\it et al.} [Phys. Rev. Res. {\bf 8}, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

papers.title: Moiré Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet
papers.summary: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moiré Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling ν_h=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moiré Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.

papers.title: Torsional Hall Viscosity of Massive Chern Insulators: Finite Temperature and Chemical Potential
papers.summary: We study the torsional Hall viscosity $ζ_{\rm H}$ of Chern insulators at finite temperature and chemical potential. Our analysis considers the massive Dirac fermion and two deformations: a constant out-of-plane magnetic field and a momentum-dependent mass described by the single-block Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hamiltonian. For the massive Dirac theory, we show that temperature and chemical potential lead to UV-finite corrections and that a chemical potential outside the bulk gap modifies $ζ_{\rm H}$ even at zero temperature. In a constant magnetic field, the response of massive Dirac fermions is dictated by the relativistic Landau-level spectrum, leading to a plateau structure at zero temperature that is smoothed at finite temperature. The jumps are proportional to the Dirac mass and inversely proportional to the squared magnetic length and the newly occupied Landau-level energy. Finally, we present a detailed study of the correction to $ζ_{\rm H}$ in the single-block BHZ continuum model due to temperature and chemical potential. For parameters relevant to (Hg,Mn)Te quantum wells, the magnitude of the jump across a mass domain wall retains its vacuum enhancement due to the BHZ deformation as long as the chemical potential lies sufficiently deep inside the gap compared with the thermal energy. Our results extend the theory of torsional Hall viscosity to experimentally relevant conditions and may facilitate its future detection.

papers.title: Interaction Landscapes of Structurally Distorted Toroidal Classical Spin Textures
papers.summary: We develop a classical discrete magnetostatic model of localized magnetic moments arranged in a toroidal texture, where the moments are represented by static current loops and study the behavior of the magnetic dipole-dipole interaction under several types of structural deformations. The purpose is to disentangle effects due to geometric and magnetic deformations, including elliptical, lopsided, alternating, and tilted configurations. In particular, we investigate how distortions modify the toroidal moment and the interaction energy between pairs of toroidal structures. The resulting interaction landscapes exhibit characteristic symmetry patterns and anisotropies that are highly sensitive to the underlying deformation. As a separate proof-of-concept comparison, first-principles calculations on a molecular spin-toroidal system reveal qualitatively similar orientation-dependent behavior. The calculated interaction is microscopically the conventional pairwise magnetic dipole-dipole interaction between localized moments arranged in a spin-toroidal texture; the toroidal moment characterizes the collective texture and should not be interpreted as introducing an additional elementary interaction term. Our results provide a platform for exploring orientation-dependent interactions of spin-toroidal textures in molecular magnets and related nanoscale magnetic systems that are essential to understand the role of toroidal order.

papers.title: Large-scale Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations with Atomic Cluster Expansion potentials in LAMMPS
papers.summary: Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics (MCMD) simulations are widely used to study the properties of materials at the mesoscale. Simulations with hundreds of thousands of atoms usually rely on empirical potentials because MCMD with machine-learning interatomic potentials is impractical at this scale in existing implementations. Here, we introduce a hybrid MPI/OpenMP scheme for MCMD with Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) potentials in LAMMPS. Monte Carlo moves are evaluated from local energy changes and carried out in parallel over MPI ranks, while molecular dynamics is parallelized over OpenMP threads. At a fixed number of CPUs, the wall time of the Monte Carlo moves decreases by a factor equal to the number of MPI ranks. Larger simulation cells also reduce the statistical errors of free energy calculations because thermal fluctuations decrease with system size. We demonstrate the scheme by calculating free energies of the HCP and BCC phases in the strongly anharmonic Hf--Ti system and by simulating zirconium segregation in a nanocrystalline copper sample of 670,000 atoms. For Cu--Zr, an ACE potential and an empirical potential predict similar grain boundary compositions but different amounts of zirconium dissolved in the grains. The scheme makes MCMD simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials practical at the length scales of microstructure.

papers.title: Orbital-dependent electronic correlations and single-band character in layered palladates
papers.summary: Layered palladates provide a $4d$ platform for examining electronic correlations in materials with cuprate-like structural and orbital characteristics. Using fully charge-self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the orbital- and layer-resolved electronic structures of LaPdO$_2$, RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$, La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$, and La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$. Under the conditions studied, all compounds remain metallic, with low-energy states dominated by the Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. This orbital exhibits stronger mass renormalization than the Pd-$d_{z^2}$ orbital. LaPdO$_2$ and BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ show moderate correlations, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ is more weakly correlated. Both the trilayer La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$ and quadlayer La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$ remain weakly correlated, with similar Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ mass enhancements and little difference between inner- and outer-layer Pd sites. Among the structures studied, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ is closest to a cuprate-like single-band description, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ retains an additional electron pocket with Pd-$d_{z^2}$ character. These results establish a comparative picture of weak to moderate, orbital-dependent electronic correlations in layered palladates.

papers.title: Out-of-training properties in frozen interatomic potential embeddings are decodable and ordered by physical scale
papers.summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on energies, forces and stresses, yet their frozen representations can predict other materials properties. We probe ORB-v3 and UMA-S across layers, read-outs and equivariant channels for nine properties of 154,875 Materials Project crystals. Both models outperform composition-only descriptors on all targets, including five outside their training objectives; errors in physical units help assess potential screening applications. Optimal depth varies by property, consistent with a physical-scale ordering. Random-weight controls reveal strongly property-dependent benefits of pretraining. UMA-S's rotation-invariant angular channels improve crystal-system classification, while higher scores from its full tensor disappear under rotation; matched-model controls do not isolate equivariance as the explanation. Accuracy varies across different probes, but nearest-neighbour prediction often approaches XGBoost performance, even though materials do not form distinct clusters according to their properties. We also test whether a linear predictor trained on one model's embeddings can predict properties using the other model's embeddings after a learned linear transformation. Predictive accuracy is largely preserved, despite differences in which atoms the two models place close together. These results guide the reuse of frozen MLIP representations for materials prediction.

papers.title: Reversal of dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven multimode optomechanical resonators
papers.summary: Dynamical backaction describes how a driven cavity field responds with delay to mechanical motion, and can be used to cool that motion toward its quantum ground state or amplify it into self-oscillation. Control over this interaction underpins laser cooling, high-fidelity state preparation, quantum transduction, and phonon lasing. In conventional cavity optomechanics, both the sign and the magnitude of the optical damping are dictated by the laser detuning, and cooling is bounded by quantum backaction (QBA), the optomechanical analogue of the Doppler limit in cold atoms. We show, in theory and experiment, that dynamical backaction can be strongly enhanced in multimode optomechanical resonators driven by time-varying (Floquet) optical fields. A modulated drive couples a sideband-unresolved MHz mode to a sideband-resolved GHz mode through the shared cavity, replacing the QBA limit of the target mode by the occupancy of the auxiliary mode. Experimentally, we cool the MHz mode to $47 \pm 13$ phonons, about half its single-mode QBA limit and an order of magnitude below what single-tone backaction reaches at the same intracavity photon number. The character of the interaction can moreover be completely inverted at fixed laser detuning, turning cooling into amplification and vice versa, controlled solely by the modulation frequency. Floquet driving thus extends open-loop quantum control, which requires no measurement or feedback, to mechanical resonators outside the resolved-sideband regime.

papers.title: The $N$-channel white-noise Schrödinger operator in all three Dyson classes. I. Explicit stationary admittance distribution, density of states and outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals
papers.summary: We obtain an explicit stationary distribution of the matrix Riccati variable---the boundary admittance---for an $N$-channel Schrödinger operator with Gaussian white-noise disorder, in all three Dyson symmetry classes $β=1,2,4$. Uniform absorption regularizes the Riccati dynamics, and the distribution's normalization factorizes into outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals. This gives a common route to the density of states and the sum of Lyapunov exponents, extending Halperin's scalar solution to coupled channels. Exact finite-$N$ formulas connect two spectral regimes: the Lifshitz tail, including its symmetry-dependent prefactor, and the collective large-$N$ edge. We reduce the $β=4$ and even-$N$ $β=1$ problems to unitary orthogonal polynomials and an auxiliary recursion. Their critical double-scaling limit yields edge profiles on the $N^{-4/5}$ energy scale, governed by a complex Painlevé-I tritronquée solution and a linear auxiliary equation. We conjecture that these profiles describe a universal edge regime of random band matrices.

papers.title: Large pseudo-orbital magnetic moment of magnons in CrI$_3$ nanotubes
papers.summary: Recently discovered CrI$_3$ nanotubes are expected to host unusual radial magnetic order states, on account of the strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy of the two-dimensional parent material. The detection of these peculiar magnetic states is challenging, and motivates the quest for unique features that can be probed experimentally. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show that an axial magnetic field tilts the radial phase into a conical one that threads the tube with an Aharonov-Bohm flux for magnons. This flux endows magnons with a pseudo-orbital magnetic moment, reaching approximately six Bohr magnetons, three times conventional magnon spin moment, and therefore detectable through magnon spectroscopy, providing a smoking gun for the radial and conical magnetic order in CrI$_3$ nanotubes.

papers.title: A Hierarchically Compressed Immittance Operator Formulation for Fast Statics-to-Full-Wave Electromagnetic Simulation with the Boundary Element Method
papers.summary: The boundary element method allows the electromagnetic simulation of three-dimensional problems with a two-dimensional discretization, using a surface integral representation of Maxwell's equations. For applications involving broadband simulations or multiscale geometries, the well-known low-frequency breakdown of conventional integral equation formulations must be addressed, while ensuring that dielectric, semiconducting, and lossy metallic regions are modeled rigorously, including the skin effect. In this work, a new boundary element formulation based on an immittance operator is proposed, where the underlying integral equations are inherently valid from statics to the full-wave regime. To enable efficient matrix assembly and solution, a hierarchical matrix compression strategy is devised, leveraging fast direct factorization as an intermediate step, and fast matrix-vector products for the iterative solution of the final system of equations. The proposed formulation is capable of electrostatic, magnetostatic, quasistatic, and full-wave simulations of dielectrics, semiconductors, and lossy metals. Representative numerical examples drawn from a variety of applications demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

papers.title: Bias Conditioning and Long-Range Electrostatics for Consistent Machine-Learning Potentials of Electrified Interfaces
papers.summary: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) of electrified interfaces need the bias as input, but it is unclear whether a scalar electrode charge suffices and whether short-range models capture the non-local response. We add charge and field conditioning to short- and long-range MLIPs. State-of-the-art field-conditioned short-range models overpolarize thick water films nearly twofold and miss work-function shifts at stepped Pt. Our long-range model captures both, needs only the electrode charge at metals as input, and reproduces ab initio simulations of the Pt(111)--water interface.

papers.title: Hund physics in the quarter-filled two-band Hubbard-Kanamori model: Crystal-field splitting and non-local Correlations
papers.summary: We address the effect of crystal-field splitting and non-local correlations in the quarter-filled two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model. The role of the Hund's coupling in this configuration is not obvious since the atomic ground state has only one electron per site. Yet, previous works identified fingerprints of the Hund's coupling defining a weak Hund's metal at least at finite temperature. Using single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) and two-site cellular DMFT based on a selected configuration-interaction solver we investigate the zero-temperature properties of the weak Hund's metal. Within DMFT we draw the boundary for the weak Hund's metal, which is consistent with previous finite-temperature results. Interestingly, we find that the fingerprints of the Hund's coupling are quite robust to the lifting of the orbital degeneracy and they survive up to splittings of a quarter of the bandwidth, well beyond those at which a two-stage Kondo screening disappears. Including non-local correlations in cluster DMFT demonstrates the robustness of the single-site DMFT picture, even if Mott localization occurs at smaller interactions. In the metal the intersite correlations are weak and insensitive to $J$, while in the localized state we find nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic, antiferro-orbital correlations that are manifest also in the mutual information between sites.

papers.title: A tunable multi-gated platform for superlattice engineering in bilayer graphene
papers.summary: Periodic potentials with length scales much larger than crystal lattice constants can generate low-energy electronic minibands. While small-angle twisted van der Waals heterostructures have been widely used to realize such physics, correlated phases are often limited by twist-angle inhomogeneity, strain, and disorder. Here, we investigate high-quality Bernal bilayer graphene placed on a patterned graphite gate, featuring a triangular array of holes, forming a new class of "gate-engineered" superlattices tunable through three independent electrostatic gates. Near the charge neutrality point, we observe insulating states characteristic of miniband formation. Temperature-dependent transport reveals activated gaps consistent with theory, and Hall measurements indicate charge-carrier inversion. Notably, the superlattice can be reconfigured electrostatically using various gate combinations, enabling flexible band-structure design without mechanical twisting. The results highlight a new route to band engineering, potentially extendable to complex periodic structures that are untenable in natural materials.

papers.title: Transferable neural-network preconditioners for Wilson--Clover propagator inversions
papers.summary: We investigate two single--layer neural-network architectures for accelerating four-dimensional Wilson--Clover propagator inversions on lattice ensembles in practical use; both transfer directly without retraining. The first is a gauge-covariant parallel transport convolution (PTC) network that directly reduces the number of generalized conjugate residual (GCR) solver iterations. The second is a CNN-like network used together with a multigrid-inspired algorithm. The two approaches can be combined to further reduce GCR iterations. PTC transfers without retraining across lattice volumes, lattice spacings, and pion masses while maintaining comparable acceleration, whereas the CNN-like network transfers directly from small- to large-volume ensembles with strong acceleration. A cost comparison accounting for both basis construction and solves shows that the proposed scheme is more advantageous for large-volume ensembles than for small-volume ones.

papers.title: A Soft Sponge-Pillar Electrode Platform for Motion-Tolerant Ambulatory EEG and Sleep Monitoring
papers.summary: Long-term wearable electrophysiological recording systems are essential for both clinical and real-world environments. While a wide range of wearable devices have been reported for electrocardiogram (ECG) and electromyogram (EMG) recording applications, most electroencephalography (EEG) measurements still require subjects to remain stationary while wearing rigid and uncomfortable equipment. Here, a soft and wearable sponge pillar EEG electrode is presented for long-term and motion-tolerant EEG recording. The electrode is composed of two layers of a carbon black (CB)-polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composite, where a firmer solid base assists in bypassing hair, enabling stable access to the scalp, while a porous sponge tip ensures comfort, reliable contact, and low skin-electrode impedance. Fabricated via a sugar templating process without microfabrication steps, the microporous sponge structure offers low modulus and significantly enhances the contact area with the skin when loaded with conductive gel. This allows the electrode to achieve a lower contact impedance of $1.62 \times 10^{4}\,Ω$ at 10 Hz, outperforming conventional gelled electrodes while maintaining gel stability for over 18 hours. With the electrodes integrated into wearable form factors such as headbands, headphones, and baseball caps, EEG signal recording during motion have been demonstrated, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 16.46 dB. These features establish the sponge pillar electrode as a promising platform for next generation wearable EEG systems, enabling comfortable, stable, and prolonged brain signal acquisition on ambulatory subjects and in naturalistic environments.

papers.title: Global bound-state spectrum and spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement in an inverse-$3/2$ magnetic quantum dot
papers.summary: We investigate the bound-state spectrum and confinement thresholds of a two-dimensional electron governed by the Schrödinger--Pauli equation in an inverse-$3/2$ radial magnetic-field profile. The radial problem reduces to the biconfluent Heun equation, but instead of restricting the solution to the quasi-exact polynomial sector, we impose the bound-state condition globally through a spectral Wronskian between the endpoint-selected Frobenius solution and the subdominant asymptotic solution. The resulting spectrum contains continuous nonpolynomial bound-state branches on which the known quasi-exact solutions appear as isolated exact points. In this global description, the polynomial index $N$ remains a termination index within the quasi-exact sector but does not uniquely label the spectral branches. An independent exact analysis of the continuum edge yields spin- and angular-momentum-dependent critical couplings that can lie below the quasi-exact restriction $U_0a>4$, where $U_0$ is the Coulomb-strength parameter and $a$ is the magnetic-profile length scale. These results establish quasi-exact solvability as a set of special analytic points embedded in a broader biconfluent-Heun spectrum with spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement thresholds.

papers.title: Altermagnetism in moiré quasicrystals
papers.summary: Altermagnetism is a collinear compensated magnetic phase with zero net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin polarization. Quasicrystalline altermagnetism extends altermagnetism beyond periodic crystals, with noncrystallographic symmetries allowing high-order spin polarization patterns. Here, we propose a symmetry-based approach to realizing quasicrystalline altermagnetism by twisting collinear magnetic layers. Specifically, we demonstrate that the $30^{\circ}$-twisted honeycomb lattice bilayers form the dodecagonal quasicrystals supporting an $i$-wave altermagnetic phase. We further find that $45^{\circ}$-twisted bilayers preserving fourfold rotational symmetry support a mirror-driven $l$-wave phase with eight nodal lines. We characterize these altermagnetic patterns through plane-wave-projected spin-resolved spectral functions and spin-resolved conductances. Our work provides a systematic route to high-angular-order quasicrystalline altermagnetism through twist engineering.

papers.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
papers.summary: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.

papers.title: Model-free stiffness measurement of microscale soft contacts by far-field traction force microscopy
papers.summary: The microscale stiffness of soft materials governs their contact mechanics, adhesion and friction, yet it is surprisingly difficult to measure. Micro or nanoindentation is typically used, but extracting stiffness from these measurements requires using contact mechanics models (e.g. JKR), whose assumptions often break down for soft adhesive contacts. Here, we introduce far-field traction force microscopy (FF-TFM) to extract stiffness without using any contact model. We drag a colloidal probe mounted on an atomic-force microscope across a soft surface, measuring the friction force while imaging the displacements of fluorescent tracers on the substrate. Far from the contact, in the elastic limit, these lateral displacements depend solely on the friction force and the substrate stiffness, and fitting them with the point-force solution thus gives the substrate's Young's modulus directly. We successfully match bulk rheology moduli with FF-TFM for six different silicone elastomers, where JKR fits to indentation data underestimate moduli by as much as 40\% of their bulk values. Our approach also enables tracking how the probe slips across the surface. We find that soft contacts can "pre-slip" with no detectable signature in the force signal, unlike stiffer contacts. FF-TFM thus offers a contact-model-free route to measuring microscale stiffness and slip behavior in soft materials.

papers.title: How Elasticity and Chiral Damping Shape Domain-Wall Creep
papers.summary: Asymmetric domain-wall expansion in the creep regime provides an experimentally accessible probe of the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) and, in principle, chiral damping. However, severe discrepancies with complementary measurement techniques and the lack of a model describing the full experimental phenomenology of the creep of chiral domain walls, limits the application of these measurements. Here, using a symmetry decomposition of the velocity curve, we derive an analytical model describing the coupled influence of domain-wall stiffness and chiral damping in the creep regime. Their interplay generates the antisymmetric distortion that shifts the velocity minimum away from the DMI field. Applied to Co-based magnetic multilayers, the model yields iDMI values consistent with BLS and flow-regime benchmarks and identifies the reasons for the longstanding discrepancy. The model provides insights for possible strategies to measure chiral damping via creep dynamics of domain walls.

papers.title: Noise-induced manifolds: reduction of slow--fast SDEs to switching processes
papers.summary: When constituents copy one another, as in reaction networks, collective behaviour and opinion dynamics, the noise of copying vanishes at consensus and can make a system bistable. More generally this noise vanishes on whole manifolds, along which slower variables keep moving and set the switching rates, yet no general method derives these switching dynamics. Here we reduce slow--fast stochastic differential equations whose fast noise acts in a single direction to a switching diffusion or piecewise-deterministic Markov process (PDMP), using the absorption probabilities of the fast noise in place of an invariant measure, and derive a first-order correction for the finite duration of switches. For the two-species Togashi--Kaneko model the reduction recovers our earlier PDMP, and the correction captures how the stationary composition depends on the timescale separation. In a model of foraging ants with a depleting food source, the hazard of leaving a source rises through every stay, which makes the colony unlikely to leave a source soon after arriving there.

papers.title: Non-Hermitian edge accretion
papers.summary: Under the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), it is generally taken for granted that the open boundary condition (OBC) spectrum is encircled by the periodic boundary condition (PBC) spectrum. Intuitively, this is because boundaries tend to block the directed NHSE amplification, thereby suppressing $\operatorname{Im}(E)$. In this work, we analytically and numerically demonstrate how this conventional scenario can be dramatically violated: In a phenomenon which we term non-Hermitian edge accretion (NHEA), strongly coupled competing NHSE channels conspire to amplify a state whenever it bounces off an edge, instead of attenuating it. This unexpected behavior arises from underappreciated consequences of non-Bloch eigenspinor orthogonality, which control the reflection coefficients as well as the balance between propagating and evanescent waves. Operating in the strongly coupled regime, NHEA is fundamentally distinct from conventional critical NHSE scaling, which is characterized by amplification feedback generated in the bulk, not the edges. Requiring only strongly coupled antagonistic NHSE chains with suitable mode orthogonality, the NHEA is platform-agnostic, and can be identified through periodically growing edge bounces in generic non-Hermitian metamaterials and quantum simulators.

papers.title: Optical writing of Dzyaloshinskii Néel-type skyrmions
papers.summary: Ultrashort laser pulses offer a route to write nanoscale topological magnetic textures for information processing. Magnetic skyrmions are prototypical examples, yet optically generating them with controlled position, type, and, in particular, chirality remains challenging. This challenge arises because magnetic dipolar interactions, which often drive skyrmion formation, preserve the degeneracy between opposite chiralities, leaving no uniquely selected spin configuration. Here, we show that in an ultrathin Co/Pt film, sequences of picosecond circularly polarized laser pulses can write Néel-type, fixed-chirality skyrmions stabilized solely by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Combining Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and magneto-optical microscopy, we comprehensively reconstruct their internal spin structure across multiple length scales, ranging from nanometres to micrometers. Using asymmetric skyrmion-expansion measurements, we determined the sign and magnitude of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and identified the written chirality. Our findings connect deterministic optical writing with the controlled spin structure of skyrmions, advancing optical control of topological textures for opto-spintronic applications.

papers.title: A simple solvable $Z_N$ Hamiltonian in any dimension
papers.summary: We construct local $Z_N$ clock Hamiltonians from Baxter-Fendley chains coupled according to an arbitrary finite oriented simple transverse graph. Bounded edge lengths and vertex degrees give finite-range multispin interactions, with $2d$-site bulk terms on a $d$-dimensional rectangular lattice. For open longitudinal boundaries, an explicit nonlocal unitary transformation decouples the chains and gives a free parafermion spectrum. On rectangular lattices this holds for any combination of open and periodic transverse boundaries. For periodic longitudinal boundaries, neighbouring chain charges fix the closing-bond twists. In each joint charge sector, the energies are sums of the corresponding twisted periodic-chain energies. As an example, we construct a three-dimensional array of chains perpendicular to a Penrose rhombus tiling.

papers.title: Parametrised-Quadratic Interface Reconstruction and Geometric Velocity Extension in the Volume-of-Fluid Framework
papers.summary: A conservative Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) framework using local parametric-curve interface reconstruction (PI-VOF) is developed for geometric interface propagation on fixed Cartesian grids. While VOF methods achieve conservative and second-order accurate interface advection under prescribed velocity fields, normal-velocity-driven interface propagation requires the interfacial velocity to be extended to neighbouring staggered-grid locations. Existing studies on interface evolution employ auxiliary distance functions, kernel smoothers, or high-resolution VOF in multiple grids to compute propagation velocities and address first-order-accuracy limitations. In contrast, PI-VOF directly employs higher-order parametric interface geometry for local normal-velocity extension, aiming to achieve second-order accurate interface evolution on fixed Cartesian grids. The resulting velocity field is employed in conservative geometric advection using a directionally split Eulerian-implicit and Lagrangian-explicit (EI-LE) scheme, while the reconstructed interface provides the geometric information required for curvature evaluation and the ghost-fluid finite-difference discretisation of sharp interfacial Dirichlet conditions. Static reconstruction and reversible-vortex advection tests demonstrate higher-order interface geometry and approximately second-order transport convergence, with mass conservation to the chosen tolerance on refined grids. Prescribed normal-velocity and curvature-dependent propagation tests establish near second-order convergence. Coupled Stefan benchmarks involving capillarity and attachment kinetics demonstrate approximately second-order thermal convergence and decreasing interface errors under mesh refinement. The results establish a geometric formulation connecting conservative VOF transport, local normal-velocity extension, and sharp Stefan conditions for evolving interfaces.

papers.title: Solubility and Diffusion of Hydrogen Isotopes and Helium in Molten FLiBe
papers.summary: Tritium produced in molten 2LiF-BeF$_2$ (FLiBe) may dissolve as T$_2$ or as TF, which differ greatly in solubility. Permeation experiments give a solubility close to that of HF and a flux proportional to the square root of the T$_2$ pressure, which has usually been taken as evidence of dissociation. We have developed a fixed-charge classical potential for FLiBe containing atomic tritium, T$_2$, TF, the hydride ion T$^-$ and helium, fitted only to periodic DFT calculations for hydrogen. The nuclei are classical, so the solubilities apply to all hydrogen isotopes. The host reproduces the measured density and neutron structure factor but is too fluid close to the liquidus. The calculated solubilities of T$_2$ and TF agree with experiment, and neither molecule dissociates in the melt. Because TF is much more soluble, it holds most of the dissolved tritium unless the salt is strongly reducing, and at constant redox potential its concentration varies with the square root of the T$_2$ pressure, which accounts for the permeation results without dissociation. Helium does not change the solubility of T$_2$: a helium bubble in the melt takes up T$_2$ as its Henry constant predicts, while TF is enriched at the bubble surface. T$_2$ diffuses somewhat faster than measured, and TF and T$^-$ two to three times more slowly than T$_2$.
